faqSection.title: FAQ
faqSection.heading: The things people usually ask
faqSection.description: Short answers to the real hesitations. If your question is not here, the free Snapshot is the simplest way to get a straight answer.

items.question: Can we hire you for just one thing, or do we have to buy everything?
items.answer: Either works. You can start with one practice, like brand or events, and add the others when it makes sense. Many clients begin with one piece and grow into the full system once they see how the parts connect.

items.question: What size organizations do you work with?
items.answer: We work with established organizations and firms that are ready to invest in doing this well. If you're weighing whether you're a fit, the Snapshot is the simplest way to find out.

items.question: Do you only work with organizations in El Paso?
items.answer: No. We're based in El Paso and our work runs across seven states and Washington D.C., and internationally. The Snapshot and much of the work happen remotely, and we travel when the project calls for it.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: It depends on what you need and how much of the system you bring in. The Snapshot is complimentary and comes with a clear read of where you stand, so you can decide with real information before any numbers come up.

founderSection.title: Founder
founderSection.name: Bianca Cervantes
founderSection.promise: I'd rather take the calculated risk that makes you unforgettable than the safe route that keeps you floating with the average. I'll tell you what I really think, because serving the vision matters more than simply telling you what you want to hear.
note: I started Bianomics after watching too many good organizations get handed a strategy deck and left to figure out the rest. I'd been on the client side of that dynamic enough times to recognize what was missing: transparency, shared understanding, and a partner genuinely invested in the mission. Too often, we were made to feel like another contract number. Those gaps became the foundation of Bianomics and the values we still operate by. We coach, support, and build capacity within your team, so what we create together doesn't walk out the door when we do.

Our team runs lean by design, using smart systems to put more of your budget where it belongs: into the work itself. But lean doesn't mean distant. We embed ourselves as an extension of your team, the people you can call when the path shifts, the pressure hits, or the deliverables alone aren't enough. We're not here to check boxes and disappear. We're here to help carry the mission.

processSection.title: Our process
processSection.label: Our process
processSection.description: Four steps to align it. The same people through all of them. It starts with a Snapshot, a straight read of where your story, systems, and people actually stand, and ends with that same team building alongside you.

steps.heading: Start with a free Snapshot
steps.description: Tell us where you stand. A straight read on your communications or brand position. No spin.

steps.heading: We find the story
steps.description: We bring what makes you worth knowing to the surface, and we agree on where you want to be by the end of this stretch of work.

steps.heading: We build the plan
steps.description: With a customized Comms OS, one connected plan across brand, events, operations, and people, sized to what you actually need right now.

steps.heading: One team, all the way through
steps.description: The people who scoped the work are the people who do it. We build it to run without you needing us. Most partners keep us anyway.

caseStudies.heading: A curriculum built once, now running in four states

caseStudies.intro: We built the youth curriculum, then built it to travel. Georgia, New Jersey, New York, and Texas now run the same methodology under their own name. Proof that what works here works anywhere.

caseStudies.heading: A veteran program built to thaw a frozen nervous system
caseStudies.summary: From first cohort to a program running through 2027.
caseStudies.intro: We designed the curriculum, built the sales kit and partnership deck that earned it sponsor funding, and ran the press campaign that carried it into public view. Still running. Still growing.

caseStudies.heading: The workforce board that handed us the whole operation
caseStudies.summary: Staff development and youth readiness, backed by the infrastructure to run it without us.
caseStudies.intro: Continuation of brand strategy, communications guidelines, a mapped consumer journey, and the project management systems underneath all of it. Not a workshop vendor. A comms department they didn't have to build themselves.

caseStudies.heading: A nonprofit trained to run its own comms, not rent ours forever

caseStudies.heading: Built by Ability, told the way it deserved to be told

caseStudies.intro: We supported the production campaign end to end and ran the public relations alongside it, so the work and the story of the work moved at the same pace.

snapshotLandingPage.title: Snapshot page (/snapshot)
snapshotLandingPage.headingRest: An honest look at where you stand.
snapshotLandingPage.intro: Tell us where you are. We read your communications and brand position and tell you what is actually working, what is not, and what we would do about it.
assurances: Read by the people who would do the work
snapshotLandingPage.coverIntro: Not a pitch deck with your logo on it. A straight read you can act on whether you work with us or not.

coverItems.heading: Where your position actually lands
coverItems.body: What people take away from your brand and communications right now, against what you intended them to take away.

coverItems.heading: The gaps costing you the most
coverItems.body: The two or three places where the work is losing you attention, credibility, or money, in the order we would fix them.

coverItems.heading: Which practices you actually need
coverItems.body: An honest read on whether this is a Vision Lab problem, a Blueprint problem, a Stage problem, or a Groundwork one. Often it is fewer than you think.

coverItems.heading: A shape for the work
coverItems.body: What a first stretch of work would cover, who from our team would do it, and roughly what it would take.

coverItems.heading: The same people, start to finish
coverItems.body: The people who read your Snapshot are the people who would do the work. No handoff, no new faces once you sign.

coverItems.heading: Yours to keep, regardless
coverItems.body: Everything in the read is yours. Use it with us, with someone else, or on your own. It is useful by design, not conditional on you signing.

snapshotLandingPage.faqIntro: The things people check before they send one in.

faqItems.question: Who is a Snapshot for?
faqItems.answer: Organizations that have built something real and know it is not landing the way it should. Founders, people leaders, and operators, mostly. If you are looking for a cheap logo refresh, we are not your people.

faqItems.question: Is it actually free? What is the catch?
faqItems.answer: It is free, and there is no catch. We take a limited number each month because every one is read personally, which is also why we ask a few questions before saying yes.

faqItems.question: What should I have ready?
faqItems.answer: Nothing formal. A link to your site or socials and a straight answer about what a win looks like in the next 90 days is enough. The more candid you are, the more useful the read.

faqItems.question: How quickly will I hear back?
faqItems.answer: Within three business days. If we are not the right fit, we will say so plainly and point you somewhere better where we can.

snapshotLandingPage.closingBody: Send it in and we will take a proper look. No retainers, no pressure, no deck with your logo pasted on the front.

members.name: Bianca Cervantes
bio: Bianca did not want to build another agency. She wanted to build the thing that fixes what agencies get wrong. Bianomics is that answer. An embedded team that stays until you no longer need us.

She thinks in nervous systems, paying attention to what is actually driving behavior, not just what is on the surface. She never sits still on an idea either. The moment one lands, she is already three ideas past it, looking for the version that is bigger and better.
Off the clock, she is always moving. Golf, gym, yoga, running. She will stop for live music, blues to house to EDM, and she will always stop for a dog.
Her favorite title is not CEO. It is Mom, to her daughter Ava. That one runs the show.

members.name: Desiree Delgado
bio: Dez does not wait for growth to happen. She goes out and builds it, one real connection at a time.
Years in hospitality taught her how to read a room fast and turn a first conversation into a relationship worth keeping. Now she runs that same instinct at scale, across an entire region's pipeline.
Across the Southwest region, she is the outreach, the pipeline, the relationships that turn into retainers.

Her fuel source is simple. 5am circuit workouts and an Alani in hand to start the day, a country karaoke session she never turns down, and a new food spot always worth trying. Koko, her 20 pound Frenchie, runs the household like she pays the rent. Order everywhere, even off the clock.

members.name: Milan Petojevic
bio: Milan catches Bianca's ideas at a hundred miles an hour and turns them into a system that makes Bianomics flow. Nobody else in the building can do that quite like him.

He is built for chaos. Genuinely loves untangling it, which is exactly how he ended up the systems guy. Night owl. Obsessive researcher. Real estate nerd. Lifelong dog person. Ask him one innocent question and he will vanish for three hours and reappear with a full analysis and a spreadsheet nobody asked for. That is just how his brain runs.
He works best quietly, in the background, solving problems before anyone even knows they exist. Usually with his dog, Lea, right by his side.

members.name: Hamna Arif
bio: Hamna is the reason nothing falls through the cracks. Timelines, deliverables, a dozen moving pieces, she keeps it all on track and keeps the team one step ahead of the deadline.
She does not just manage the chaos, she quietly fixes what causes it. She spots the clunky process before anyone else does and smooths it out so the rest of the team can move faster.
Off the clock, she is chasing sunsets, good food, and good tea. Music is always on. Cats over most humans, no argument there.

members.name: Pavle Maodus
bio: Pavle's first computer session was at age 3, back in 2007. Nearly two decades later, he is a master of web design, moving fast across sites, automations, and SEO through his own studio, fast enough that clients keep forgetting he is only 22.

Four languages, three modes: zen, focus, deal-closer, whichever the moment calls for. He also helps run his family's alcohol distilling business on the side, because clearly one job was never going to be enough for him.

House music never turns off, and neither does his love for cinematography, history, and proper European pub culture with friends once the weekend hits. Work hard, play hard is not a slogan for him, it is the whole operating system.

members.name: Chris Lechuga
bio: Chris has spent 15 years helping schools, nonprofits, and coalitions tell the truth about their work in ways people actually listen to. El Paso native, national public affairs consultant, and a rockstar with PR who has the receipts, stories in The New York Times, CNBC, and CBS News, leaders coached through congressional testimony.

He has stood at the podium as a school district PIO on the worst day of the school year, and he has never lost the instinct that came from it. A good pitch works like a good riff, hook first, no filler. He chases impact, not headlines, not column inches.
He brings a rock and roll mindset to a suit-and-tie industry, and it shows. Clarity over noise, every single time.

members.name: Minerva Saucedo
bio: Minerva flips the script on healing. Self-care is not the reward at the end of it. It is where it starts. She learned that the hard way, sitting with families through the toughest parts of substance abuse, and now she teaches it for a living.
Licensed cosmetologist by trade, recovery coach at heart, she treats those two worlds like they were never separate to begin with. Small, repeatable acts of care beat willpower every time.
Off the clock, she is laughing too hard to finish her own stories, hunting down the next great food spot, and yes, she really does own an exact replica of the Grail Diary from Indiana Jones.

members.name: Greg Kruger
members.role: Nervous System Coach, US Marine veteran
bio: Greg used to think willpower was the answer. Turns out, willpower was getting way too much credit.

He spent years figuring out what was actually running the show underneath all that effort and trying harder. Once he figured it out, he fixed his own patterns, then built a career helping other people fix theirs.

U.S.M.C. veteran. Licensed NLP practitioner. Certified breathwork facilitator. Founder of Forgotten Truth Coaching. His rule is simple: leadership starts with self-leadership. Skip that part and everything else gets harder.
Inside Beyond Duty, Greg skips the motivational speech and starts with the breath. No slogans. No trying harder. Just a shift people can actually feel.
Off the clock, he is chasing waves, riding his bike, and making music. Apparently, sitting still was never really his thing.

collaborators.name: Kandolite Carson
bio: By day she is the Queen of the In-Between. By every other hour she is an ultimate boy mom. For 18 plus years, she has built brands, told stories, and turned bold ideas into real ones across journalism, PR, media, marketing, nonprofit leadership, and creative strategy.
She is professionally curious in the best way, the kind who asks one question and somehow connects five dots nobody saw coming. A crazy idea walks in, proof it should have happened sooner walks out.

Off the clock, she is training for her first triathlon, chasing two boys and a firefighter husband, and will still defend the 90s as the greatest decade pop culture ever had. Burned CDs from Limewire, included and unashamed.

collaborators.name: Vanessa Tena
bio: Nobody warns you about Vanessa. She shows up looking like a pageant queen and leaves the room wondering how she just ran policy, built a tech solution, and had everyone laughing, all before lunch. Bianomics' actual secret weapon.
Marketing, advertising, public affairs, government leadership, tech, she has worn every one of those hats and made each look like it was made for her, Telly Award and Mrs. Texas Earth crown included.
She is also a passionate advocate for kids born with hearing loss, using her own journey to help the next generation own their story and lead with confidence.
Off the clock, she is mom first, karaoke queen second, poodle mom always, Doritos never far away. Give her five minutes and she will leave you laughing and a little obsessed.

collaborators.name: Celisse Villagrana
bio: Celisse gives brands a pulse. 15+ years across creative agencies, architecture and development, and her own consulting practice, and she still treats every project like the first one. Branding, advertising, visual systems, creative direction. She runs the full range and makes it look easy.
She translates strategy into something people actually feel. Print, digital, environmental, marketing, she keeps the story consistent wherever it shows up.

Campaigns, production, stakeholders, deadlines, she holds the whole thing together without losing the thread from first concept to final execution. Fluent in English and Spanish, she has zero patience for a brand with no personality.

Off the clock, she is on the dance floor, sketchbook in hand, chasing her next stamp in her passport. Moksha the dog and Micho the cat hold down the fort while she is out being a visionary in real time.

collaborators.name: Nova Rizki Ananda
bio: Nova is Bianomics' secret weapon. Give her a rough idea and she will hand you back a brand system that actually holds together, branding, decks, print, digital, all of it clean, all of it hers.
She has an eye that catches the one detail everyone else missed, and she never turns it off. Every deck, every layout, every brand asset gets that same level of attention.
Off the clock, she is at the piano, in a book, or chasing down a new café. Same eye for detail, just pointed at the rest of life.

collaborators.name: Talha Zunair
bio: Talha turns a rough idea or a wall of text into something people actually stop and look at. Deck, brand asset, print piece, doesn't matter, he finds the version that holds attention every time.
One rule runs everything he makes. Clarity over decoration. If it doesn't support the message, it doesn't make the cut.
He is always one tool ahead of everyone else, chasing the next thing before it's cool, powered by a coffee habit that could sponsor its own brand.
